title: Rhythm Mastery

learn.summary: Rhythm is the skill that makes or breaks beginners — audiences forgive a wrong note but never a lost beat. Everything hangs on the pulse: a steady grid measured in beats per minute (most pop sits between 90 and 120 BPM). ABRSM examiners test rhythm before anything else for a reason.

do: Clap the rhythm of any song on the radio today while tapping the steady pulse with your foot — two different jobs at once.

children.title: Note Values

learn.summary: Note lengths halve as they go: one whole note = two halves = four quarters = eight eighths = sixteen sixteenths. A dot adds half the note's own value, so a dotted quarter lasts one and a half beats. Rests follow the exact same arithmetic in silence.

do: Set a metronome to 60 BPM and clap four quarters, then eight eighths, then two dotted-quarter-plus-eighth patterns without stopping.

children.title: Time Signatures

learn.summary: The top number says how many beats per bar, the bottom says which note gets one beat. 4/4 (common time) powers most pop and rock; 3/4 is the waltz; 6/8 groups six eighths into two lilting big beats, like an Irish jig or many ballads. Feel the difference in your body, not on paper.

do: Identify the time signature of five songs in your playlist by counting along — find at least one that is not in 4/4.

children.title: Counting & Clapping

learn.summary: Count eighth notes as "1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &" and sixteenths as "1 e & a". Counting aloud while clapping is not a beginner crutch — conservatory students still do it, because the voice locks the brain to the grid. If you can say it, you can play it.

do: Clap the rhythm of your favorite chorus while counting "1 & 2 &" aloud — repeat until you get through it three times cleanly.

children.title: Syncopation

learn.summary: Syncopation accents the beats you don't expect — the off-beats, the "&"s. The rock and pop backbeat (snare on beats 2 and 4) is mild syncopation; funk and Latin styles push accents onto sixteenth-note off-beats. It is the difference between music that sits and music that grooves.

do: Clap only on beats 2 and 4 along with three songs today — if you catch yourself drifting to 1 and 3, start the song over.
